title: Becoming professional: summers in Alexandria and early wages
summary: Led his own band at 15 playing a black hotel in Alexandria at fifteen dollars a week; cost of groceries.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: See even when I was in school I was playing. Because I had to take care of my family.
So at what time were you making money from music? I mean when did you consider yourself a professional musician?

When I was, but I wasn't making much, but I wasn't making as much as the other guys. But so I would say 14 or 15 years old. And like when school would close during the summer vacation I would go to either Tibbet or Alexandria to play. I had a band in Alexandria when I was 15 years old. Every summer we would take a trip and play out there. And who was this with?
Well I had my own band.
And what, and I'm trying to focus on where would you all play and what was the.

Oh in Alexandria we played at a hotel, a black hotel. They had upstairs at the hotel and downstairs there was a dance hall and like a club. And we used to play there every night. We were staying at the hotel upstairs, downstairs. We'd go down and play every night. In other words I thought that was a lot of money. We were making $15 a week.
The band or you individually? As individuals.
Wow. And see at that time musicians weren't making that kind of money.
I guess my question is why did they have to bring a band in, people from New Orleans, to play?

Oh they didn't have any, we didn't have any bands out there. There was one guy that had a band, Lil Joe. Lil Joe had a band that played but his band would travel all around northern Louisiana. And there were a couple more bands that were from Alexandria, but they were older than us and they had a bigger name than us. And they played a lot. They were older than us. And they were, they were making about $20 a week a piece. Yeah. See when you get, when you get a, now like this band, Thomas Jefferson, Adam Lambert and Famous Lambert, they had this job at the rhythm club. Oh we thought those guys were rich. The money they was making, they was making seven nights a week. They was making $21 a week. Well see back then and during those days $21 a week was a lot of money. A lot of money.

Like I used to go to the grocery stores with my mother to shop and like she'd buy a pound of rice, that was a nickel. A pound of sugar was a nickel. She wanted to get a chicken, get your live chicken, pick out the chicken you want.
And it was 15 cents for a chicken. So you can take, sometimes she would take a dollar and the whole, the five of us would eat off that for a week. Uh huh. Yeah.
